requirements.note: Inset grouped History list, newest first. Each row shows name, date, exercise count and volume on the right (e.g. Legs, Sun Oct 25, 4 exercises, 6,767.5 lb). An in-progress workout gets its own card at the top.
Detail screen shows a summary card (exercises, sets, volume), then one card per exercise listing its sets (25 lb × 13). Exercise headers push to the exercise screen.

Workout tab: name field, Add Exercise sheet (bottom search bar plus a muscle filter menu; picks one exercise per trip), per-exercise Add Set sheet with number-pad fields, prefilled from the previous set. Tapping a set edits it; swipe-to-delete works. Finish stays disabled until there is a name and a set, then adds the workout to History. No confirmation on finish.
Exercises tab lists all exercises grouped by muscle with section headers and a search field in the navigation bar.
Shows muscle and equipment, the best set (heaviest, with workout and date; updated with the new 100 lb set), and the list of workouts it appears in, which push to their details.
The in-progress workout (name, exercise, edited and deleted sets) survived relaunch. The finished workout stayed in History after relaunch.

tells: Pushed screens (workout detail, exercise detail) have an opaque white navigation bar with a hairline and a grey gap below it. iOS 26/27 uses a transparent bar with a scroll-edge effect, and A's own root screens do too.

The New Set / Edit Set sheet header is custom-drawn: plain blue 'Cancel' text, a regular-weight title, a grey capsule 'Save', and no grabber. It doesn't match the system glass toolbar buttons on the Add Exercise sheet.
Accessibility exposes rows as 'Link' elements inside nested scroll views, which suggests a web-style view hierarchy (not visible to the eye).
The exercise picker returns after each pick, so adding several exercises means reopening the sheet each time (no multi-select).
Finish has no confirmation, and there is no visible discard affordance apart from the overflow menu.
A.scroll: History scrolls smoothly with normal momentum and rubber-banding; no blank or popping rows. Scroll position is kept after pushing a detail and coming back.

requirements.note: History is grouped by month (October 2026 header), newest first. Rows show a bold name with the date on the right, and below it SF-symbol-labelled exercise count and volume. A 'Workout in Progress, Resume' card appears at the top while one is active.

Detail has a large title and a summary card (date, exercises, sets, total volume), then one card per exercise with sets (13 reps × 25 lb) and a per-exercise volume footer. A '…' menu offers Delete Workout.

The + button opens the workout: name field (defaults to 'Morning Workout'), multi-select Add Exercises sheet with search field and muscle chip filter. Add Set sheet has text fields plus steppers, a Next/Done keyboard toolbar, inline validation ('Reps must be a whole number of at least 1') and a 'Last time' hint. Tap a set to edit it (with Delete Set); swipe-to-delete works. Finish confirms and removes exercises that have no sets. Minimize returns to History with a Resume card.
Exercises tab is grouped by muscle, each row showing equipment and how many workouts use it. A search field appears on pull-down.
Shows muscle and equipment, a Best Set card with trophy (90 lb × 8 reps, Legs · Aug 9), and Workouts (3) with each workout's sets, including the newly finished one.
Relaunch reopened straight into the in-progress workout with its sets intact. The finished workout stayed in History after relaunch.

tells: After the Add Set sheet closes, focus jumps back to the workout-name field and the keyboard reappears.
While the picker's search is active, the Add (n) button is hidden until search is closed (standard iOS 26 search toolbar behaviour, but slightly awkward).
B.scroll: History and library scroll smoothly with proper momentum, rubber-band over-pull and sticky large-title collapse. Scroll position is kept on returning from a detail.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and look native in light, dark and large text. B goes further: multi-select exercise picking, steppers with validation, prefill and 'last time' hints, a finish confirmation, minimize/resume, and month-grouped history. A has a hand-drawn set-sheet header and opaque iOS-18-style navigation bars on pushed screens, which give it away; B's screens are consistent system chrome throughout.
